name: CT-01
label: Safe D

key_factors: D+12 district lean combined with a Democratic-favorable environment
Bronin's overwhelming money advantage: $3.1M raised versus about $21K for Chai, who has only $344 on hand
Open seat after Larson's primary loss, though Democrats landed a well-known nominee
model.rationale: The district's twelve-point Democratic lean, a favorable environment, and Bronin's roughly 150-to-1 fundraising edge over Chai make a Democratic hold overwhelmingly likely, with outside spending also flowing heavily toward Bronin; markets price about 95% Democratic, and the open-seat transition accounts for the small shading below the fundamentals.
model.watch: A late surge of Republican outside spending or any polling showing a single-digit race would be the main signal to revisit this rating.
notes: No expert rater lists this race; treated as safe for the party holding the seat.
No usable general-election polls; forecast rests on fundamentals and expert ratings.
Open seat: John B. Larson (D) is not on the ballot.

overview:
Connecticut's first district leans heavily Democratic, with a partisan edge of about twelve points, and the seat opened when John Larson lost renomination. Former Hartford mayor Luke Bronin enters the general as the Democratic nominee with roughly $3.1 million raised, plus more than $1.3 million in outside support. Republican Amy Chai has raised about $21,000 and reports only a few hundred dollars on hand, while a Green Party candidate also appears on the ballot.

No public general-election polls or expert ratings cover the race, so the outlook rests on district fundamentals, the stark money gap, and a Democratic-favorable environment. Prediction markets put Democratic odds near 95%. The combination of the district's lean, the fundraising disparity, and Bronin's profile points to a comfortable Democratic hold, with the open-seat transition the main source of residual uncertainty.
